'''''The Geometry of Four-Manifolds''''' is a mathematical [[textbook]] about [[Yang–Mills theory]], or more generally [[gauge theory]], and its application to the study of the geometry and topology of [[Smooth manifold|smooth]] [[4-manifold|4-manifolds]] as described by [[Donaldson theory]]. It is considered a standard work for this topic.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|access-date=2026-01-25 |author=Elmer Rees |date=2009 |language=en |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |title=Donaldson, S. K. and Kronheimer, P. B. The Geometry of Four-manifold |url=https://doi.org/10.1017/S0013091500005800}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> It was written by [[Simon Donaldson]], who received the [[Fields Medal]] in 1986 for his work in the field,<ref name=":4">{{cite web|access-date=2026-01-25 |title=Fields Medals 1986 - Donaldson, Faltings, Freedman Achievements |url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-1986}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and [[Peter Kronheimer]]. It was published on 13 September 1990 with a second revised edition in 1997.

== Content ==

''The Geometry of Four-Manifolds'' first describes the foundations of the theories of [[4-manifold|4-manifolds]] and [[Connection (principal bundle)|connections]] on [[Principal bundle|principal bundles]] as well as [[Connection (vector bundle)|connections]] on [[Vector bundle|vector bundles]].<ref>Donaldson & Kronheimer 90, Chapter 1, 2 und 5</ref> Afterwards it explains [[Yang–Mills theory]], which includes [[Uhlenbeck's singularity theorem]], the [[ADHM construction]] and the central [[Yang–Mills moduli space]], on which [[Donaldson invariant|Donaldson invariants]] are based on.<ref>Donaldson & Kronheimer 90, Chapter 2, 3, 4 und 9</ref> A special focus lies on the combination with [[complex geometry]], which includes [[Kähler manifold|Kähler manifolds]] and (stable) [[Holomorphic vector bundle|holomorphic vector bundles]].<ref>Donaldson & Kronheimer 90, Chapter 6</ref>

== Background ==

Simon Donaldson and Peter Kronheimer both obtained their [[DPhil]] at the [[University of Oxford]] under the supervision of [[Michael Francis Atiyah]], in the years 1983 and 1986 respectively. Simon Donaldson was invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) and gave plenar talks about ''Gauge theory and topology'' as well as ''Geometry of Four-Manifolds''.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2026-01-26 |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU) |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=donaldson}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

== Reviews ==

[[Elmer Rees]] wrote, the textbook is a "polished account of Donaldson's pioneering work; also included are several of the consequent developments in which he has played the leading role". Furthermore, "For someone with a good working knowledge of a range of graduate level courses, this book is self-contained."<ref name=":0" />
